info.title: Identity Cloud Management & Federation API
info.summary: Programmatic Administration API for Multi-Tenant OIDC 1.0, SAML 2.0 & macOS Touch ID Identity Providers
info.description:
REST API for programmatically provisioning and configuring Identity Providers, SAML 2.0 Service Providers (including inline SP Metadata XML import), OpenID Connect 1.0 Relying Parties, JWKS/X.509 signing keys, Shared Directory Users, and Workload JWTs.

### Authentication for External API Clients
Create a scoped **Admin API Client** in the Console (**API Clients & OpenAPI**) to obtain a `client_id` (`iac_...`) and `api_token` / `client_secret` (`idp_adm_...`). External clients can authenticate using any of:
1. **Bearer Token**: `Authorization: Bearer idp_adm_...` *(or `Authorization: ApiKey idp_adm_...`)*
2. **API Key Header**: `X-API-Key: idp_adm_...`
3. **HTTP Basic Auth**: `Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`
4. **OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials**: Exchange `client_id` + `client_secret` at `POST /api/oauth2/token` (`grant_type=client_credentials`) for a short-lived `idp_at_...` Bearer token.

An Admin API Client (and its access tokens) stops working as soon as its owner is removed from the administrator list (`users.txt`). A client with `allowed_ips` authenticates only from those addresses: from any other address its credentials get the same `401` as invalid ones, and the attempt is recorded in the owner's administrator audit log (`admin_client.source_denied`). The former per-administrator legacy API key (`Authorization: ApiKey <key>` at `POST /api/token`) is retired: it is no longer returned by the console and is accepted only while the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_ADMIN_API_KEY=1` (`legacy_admin_api_key` in config.php).

Credentials are verified before any rate limit applies, and only failures are counted, per client address: after 12 failed credential checks within 5 minutes (10 at `POST /api/oauth2/token`), further failures from that address get `429` for 5 minutes. A valid credential is never refused by this limit. A request with a console session and an `Authorization` header that is not an Admin API client credential (for example the Basic credentials of an authentication gate in front of the console) is authenticated by its session.

### Console Sessions and SCIM Credentials
The Admin Console authenticates with its session cookie (`ConsoleSession`); state-changing requests made with the cookie also need the `X-CSRF-Token` header (`ConsoleCsrfToken`, the `csrfToken` value from `/api/me`). Managing Admin API Clients and the IP allowlist status and blocked-request log accept **only** a console session: API clients get `403`. The administrator audit log (`GET /api/admin-audit-logs`) accepts a console session or an Admin API client that an administrator granted `can_read_admin_audit`. The hosted SCIM 2.0 server (`/{idpId}/scim/v2`) accepts a SCIM token (`idp_scim_...`) or an Admin API Client token (`idp_adm_...` / `idp_at_...`) that can access the provider and has `user_scope` `read` (`write` for changes), sent as `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key`; HTTP Basic and `Authorization: ApiKey` are not accepted there.

### Provider-Level Scoping
Each Admin API Client can be restricted to **one or more specific providers** (`provider_scope: "selected"`, `allowed_provider_ids: [...]`) or granted access to **all providers** (`provider_scope: "all"`), with independent read/write controls and optional `can_create_providers` auto-granting.

### Directory Access and Capabilities
`user_scope` governs everything that reads or changes the shared directory: `/api/users`, `/api/groups`, passkey deletion, and SCIM tokens and connectors (listing needs `read`; creating, changing, deleting, testing or syncing needs `write`). A SCIM token can never carry more access than its creator's `user_scope`. Password-pushing SCIM connectors can only be created or changed from the console (unless the operator sets `OIDC_ALLOW_API_CLIENT_PASSWORD_PUSH=1`). Minting JWTs at `POST /api/token`, importing private signing keys (`keyMode: "paste"`), and creating, changing or rotating the secret of an OIDC client that can use the `client_credentials` grant (its tokens carry its `client_id` as their subject) require the `can_mint_tokens` capability, which an administrator grants per client. Clients created before the capability existed do not have it (the operator can restore the old rule, under which provider `write` permission was enough, with `OIDC_LEGACY_API_CLIENT_TOKEN_MINTING=1`).

### Durations
Duration fields (`keyTtl`, `ttl`, `retention`, `leadTime`, `expires_in`, ...) take a number of seconds (`3600`) or a duration such as `90min`, `1h`, `2h30m`, `1 day` or `1w`. Values that cannot be parsed are rejected with `400`; nothing is silently replaced or clamped.

post.summary: Issue OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Access Token
post.description: Exchanges an Admin API Client `client_id` and `client_secret` for a short-lived `Bearer` token (`idp_at_...`). Credentials may be supplied via HTTP Basic auth or request body. The credentials are verified first and only failures are counted: after 10 failures within 5 minutes from one client address, further failures from it get `429` for 5 minutes. Valid credentials are never refused.

ttl.description: Token lifetime from 60 to 86400 seconds, as seconds or a duration such as `90min` or `2h`; anything else is rejected with `400 invalid_request`.
60 to 86400 seconds, as seconds or a duration such as `90min`.

429.description: Too many failed authentication attempts from this address; retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Valid credentials are still accepted.

post.summary: Sign In to the Admin Console
post.description:
Starts a console session for an administrator listed in `users.txt` and returns its CSRF token. `users.txt` entries must be password hashes (`password_hash()`, for example bcrypt or argon2id); plaintext entries are accepted only while the operator sets `OIDC_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_ADMIN_PASSWORDS=1`, and only with at least 12 characters.

**Second factor.** An administrator with an authenticator app (see `/api/admin-mfa`), or every administrator while the operator sets `OIDC_ADMIN_REQUIRE_MFA=1`, must also send the app's current 6-digit code as `otp`. Without it, a correct password answers `401` with `mfa_required: true` and starts no session. An administrator who must use an app but has none gets `mfa_enrollment_required: true` and a new `totp` secret; signing in again with a code from it confirms the app and signs in. Each code works once.

**Rate limits.** A successful sign-in sets a signed, HttpOnly known-device cookie (`__Host-IDPADMDEV` over https, `IDPADMDEV` over http) for 30 days. From a browser with that cookie, only the failures made with it count (8 per 15 minutes). Other attempts are limited per address and username (8 per 5 minutes), per account from all addresses (10 per 15 minutes), per address across all usernames (20 failures per 15 minutes) and globally (200 failures per 15 minutes, which also raises an alert in the error log and in every administrator's audit log). While a limit applies, even a correct password answers `429`; failures made elsewhere never lock an administrator out of a browser they signed in with before.

otp.description: Current code of the administrator's authenticator app, when one is required

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie and the known-device cookie are set

401.description: Invalid credentials, or the password was correct and a code from an authenticator app is needed (`mfa_required`)

429.description: Too many failed sign-in attempts or invalid codes; retry later, or from a browser that signed in before

post.summary: Sign Out the Administrator's Other Console Sessions
post.description: Console session only. Every other console session of the signed-in administrator (in other browsers or on other devices) ends at its next request; the session that sends this request stays signed in. Admin API Clients are not affected. Audited as `admin.sessions_revoked`.

200.description: The other sessions are signed out

500.description: The other sessions could not be signed out

get.description: Console session only. Whether the signed-in administrator has an authenticator app, and whether the operator requires one (`OIDC_ADMIN_REQUIRE_MFA=1`).

post.summary: Start Setting Up an Authenticator App
post.description: Console session only; needs the current `password`. Returns a new TOTP secret (RFC 6238 with SHA-1, 6 digits and 30-second steps) and its `otpauth://` URI. Confirm it within 15 minutes at `POST /api/admin-mfa/totp/confirm`; from then on every console sign-in needs a code. `409` when an app is already set up. An operator resets a lost app by deleting the administrator's row from the `admin_mfa_totp` table.

403.description: Wrong password, or not a console session

409.description: An authenticator app is already set up

delete.description: Console session only; needs the current `password` and, for a confirmed app, a current `otp`. While the operator sets `OIDC_ADMIN_REQUIRE_MFA=1`, the next sign-in sets up a new app.

403.description: Wrong password or code, or not a console session

404.description: No authenticator app is set up

429.description: Too many wrong passwords or codes

post.summary: Confirm the Authenticator App
post.description: Console session only. Activates the pending authenticator app with a current code from it.

403.description: Invalid code, expired setup, or not a console session

get.description:
A console session reads the signed-in administrator's log; an Admin API client needs `can_read_admin_audit` and reads its owner's log (other clients get `403`). Administrative events: console logins (including failed attempts with this username), Admin API client changes and secret rotations, `/api/token` mints (jti, sub, aud, exp, kid and extra claim names), provider, key, certificate, client, application, user, group, SCIM token and connector changes. Each entry names the actor (session administrator, API client or legacy key owner), source IP and user agent. Secrets are never recorded. Entries survive the deletion of the provider they concern.

Retention by `audit_class`: `security` entries (every change, sign-in, mint and alert) are kept for 365 days; beyond the newest 20000 of an administrator only entries older than 90 days are removed, so no actor can push its own recent actions out of the log. `routine` entries (`admin_client.token_issued`, one per client credentials exchange) keep the newest 2000 per administrator, and `untrusted` entries (unauthenticated failures, such as failed sign-ins with this username) the newest 500 per administrator; both expire after 90 days and never remove entries of another class.

Collecting the log (for example into a SIEM): pass `since_id=0` first, then the largest `id` received. With `since_id` the entries come oldest first and only those with a greater `id`, so no entry is skipped; an empty `logs` array means there is nothing new. Reading the log is not itself recorded.

parameters.name: since_id
parameters.description: Return the entries with a greater `id`, oldest first (at most `limit`). Without it, the newest entries come first. Anything but digits is rejected with `400`.

200.description: Audit entries: newest first, or oldest first with `since_id`

get.description:
Console session only, and only for the administrators in `ip_allowlist_admins` when the operator sets it (by default every console administrator). The IP allowlist as the server applies it: its `state` (`disabled`, `active`, or `deny_all` when every request is refused), whether it is enforcing or report-only, where it is set (`source`) and whether config.php loads; the usable ranges with their labels, and the entries it ignores (`problems`); the caller's own address and the decision the allowlist makes for it (`viewer`, with an entry that would allow it); configuration `warnings`; `trusted_proxies`; and the size and retention of the blocked-request log (entries past the retention period are deleted when this is read). No filesystem path is returned.

Ranges are never set through the API: only in config.php (`ip_allowlist`) or the `OIDC_IP_ALLOWLIST` environment variable.

403.description: Admin API clients and administrators not listed in ip_allowlist_admins

get.description:
Console session only, and only for the administrators in `ip_allowlist_admins` when the operator sets it. The requests the IP allowlist refused and, in report-only mode, those it would have refused (`enforced: false`). Each entry covers one client address (an IPv6 /64), reason, report-only state and hour: the number of requests (`hits`), the first and the last request (method and path), and the Host header and user agent of the last one, plus, behind a trusted proxy, its address and the X-Forwarded-For header. Query strings, request bodies, cookies and other headers are never stored.

JSON answers one page, newest entry first: `total` counts every entry that matches the filters, and `next_cursor`, sent back as `cursor`, fetches the next page. `format=csv` downloads every matching entry instead (`limit` and `cursor` do not apply), newest first and at most the newest 100000, as the attachment `blocked-requests-<UTC time>.csv`; cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return get a leading `'`, so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas. Every export is recorded in the administrator audit log (`ip_allowlist.log_exported`).

Entries whose last request is older than `ip_allowlist_log_retention_days` (default 30) are deleted, and the log never grows past `ip_allowlist_log_max_mb` (default 32 MiB): when it is full, the oldest entries make room.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block: entries whose address is inside it. IPv6 is matched per /64 (entries are kept per /64), so an IPv6 address or a prefix longer than /64 matches its whole /64.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Entries whose last request is at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time (UTC unless it has an offset), or Unix seconds.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Entries whose first request is at or before this time, in the formats of `since`.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: `not_listed`: the address is outside every range; `bad_forwarded_for`: a trusted proxy sent a malformed X-Forwarded-For header (or more than 32 hops or 4096 bytes); `unknown_address`: the connection's address (REMOTE_ADDR) is not an IP address; `config_error`: no entry is usable, or config.php sets `ip_allowlist` but does not load; `check_failed`: the check itself failed.

parameters.name: enforced
parameters.description: `1`: refused requests; `0`: report-only entries (requests that were served and would have been refused).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page (JSON only).

200.description: One page of entries, newest first, or with `format=csv` every matching entry as a CSV attachment

next_cursor.description: Send as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page

schema.description: UTF-8 CSV with the header row `id,hour_start_utc,first_seen_utc,last_seen_utc,hits,address,address_key,peer_address,forwarded_for,reason,enforced,first_method,first_path,last_method,last_path,host,user_agent`; times are UTC and `enforced` is `1` or `0`.

403.description: Admin API clients and administrators not listed in ip_allowlist_admins

delete.description: Console session only, and only for the administrators in `ip_allowlist_admins` when the operator sets it. Needs the current `password` of the signed-in administrator, so a borrowed session cannot wipe the record (`403` when it is wrong, `429` after 5 wrong passwords within 15 minutes). Send exactly one of `all: true`, which deletes every entry, or at least one filter (`ip`, `since`, `until`, `reason`, `enforced`, as for `GET`), which deletes the matching entries; both or neither answer `400`. Audited as `ip_allowlist.log_purged`, with the scope, the filters and the number of entries deleted.

password.description: Current console password of the signed-in administrator

all.description: `true` deletes every entry; send no filter with it

ip.description: Entries of this IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block (IPv6 per /64)

since.description: Entries whose last request is at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time, or Unix seconds

until.description: Entries whose first request is at or before this time, in the formats of `since`

403.description: Wrong password, missing or wrong CSRF token, cross-origin request, Admin API client, or an administrator not listed in ip_allowlist_admins

get.description: Returns all Identity Providers accessible to the caller (automatically filtered to `allowed_provider_ids` when called by a provider-scoped API client).

post.summary: Create Identity Provider
post.description: Creates a new OIDC 1.0 + SAML 2.0 Identity Provider. Requires `provider_scope='all'` or `can_create_providers=true` (when `provider_scope='selected'`, the newly created provider is automatically added to the API client's `allowed_provider_ids`). The provider ID (`idpId`, used in every public URL) is global and built from the owner's username and the provider name: `<owner>-<name>`, percent-encoded, with every `-` of the name replaced by `_` (`staging-idp` gives `admin-staging_idp`), so the owner is always the part before the last `-` and no administrator can take an ID that another administrator's provider names would produce. Providers created earlier keep their ID; the operator can restore the old IDs (the name's `-` kept) with `OIDC_LEGACY_PROVIDER_ID_FORMAT=1`. A name whose ID equals another provider's ID, ignoring case and percent-encoding, is rejected with `409`. Importing a private key (`keyMode: "paste"`) requires `can_mint_tokens` for API clients.

409.description: Provider name already exists, or a provider with this ID already exists

get.description: Tells whether the caller already has a provider with this name, or whether the ID a new provider with this name would get is already taken by any provider. `idpId` is that ID.

idpId.description: ID a provider created with this name would get (empty for an empty name)

400.description: `default_auth_policy` missing or not one of the listed values

patch.summary: Set Signing Key TTL (automatic rotation interval)

ttl.description: At least 300 seconds and at most 365 days. A non-zero rotation lead time must stay at least 300 seconds shorter than the TTL.

patch.summary: Set How Long Expired Keys Stay Published

retention.description: 0 to 365 days. A key also stays published until every token it signed has expired.

leadTime.description: 0, or at least 300 seconds shorter than the key TTL: automatic rotation generates a new key every TTL minus lead time, and that interval may not be shorter than 300 seconds.

patch.description: Updates one or more provider-level settings (`default_auth_policy`, `key_ttl`, `expired_key_retention`, `key_rotation_lead_time`, `active_kid`) in a single request. The key TTL must be at least 300 seconds, and a non-zero rotation lead time must stay at least 300 seconds shorter than it (automatic rotation generates a new key every TTL minus lead time). Setting `active_kid` also sets the provider `alg` to that key's algorithm.

post.summary: Parse SAML 2.0 SP Metadata XML
post.description: Parses a raw `<md:EntityDescriptor>` Service Provider XML document and extracts Entity ID, ACS URLs, signing/encryption X.509 certificates, NameID formats, and `<md:RequestedAttribute>` mappings.

post.summary: Create SAML 2.0 Application (Explicit JSON or Inline SP Metadata XML)
post.description: Creates a SAML 2.0 Service Provider integration. You may either supply explicit fields (`name`, `sp_entity_id`, `acs_url`, ...) OR pass `sp_metadata_xml` with optional overrides (e.g. `auth_policy: "touchid_only"`).

get.summary: Get Provider SAML 2.0 Signing Certificate & IdP Metadata XML
get.description:
Returns the active certificate, every certificate of the provider (`certs`, each with `state` `active`, `next` or `retired` and `retired_at`), hosted metadata URLs, and the IdP metadata XML. The metadata lists the active certificate first, then a staged (`next`) certificate and certificates retired within the last 30 days, so SPs can roll over.

`active_cert` and every entry of `certs` carry their expiry status: `expired` (boolean), `expires_in_days` (whole days left, negative once expired; null when the expiry is unknown) and `expires_soon` (not expired and under 30 days left, or under a third of the validity period for a certificate valid for less than 90 days). An expired active certificate keeps signing, so SPs that pinned it keep working; rotate it.

200.description: Active SAML X.509 certificate, all certificates with their states and expiry status, hosted metadata URLs, and raw IdP Metadata XML

post.summary: Create a New Provider SAML 2.0 X.509 Signing Certificate
post.description: By default the new certificate is staged as `next`: it is published in the metadata but signs nothing until it is activated (`POST .../saml-certs/{certId}/activate`), so SPs can import it first. With `activate: true` it signs at once; the previous certificate becomes `retired` and stays published for 30 days. An earlier staged certificate is retired.

activate.description: Sign with the new certificate immediately instead of staging it as `next`

201.description: The new certificate (`state` is `next`, or `active` with `activate: true`)

post.summary: Activate a Staged or Recently Retired SAML Certificate
post.description: Makes a `next` certificate, or one retired less than 30 days ago, the active signing certificate; the current one becomes `retired`. Expired certificates, and certificates whose private key has been removed, cannot be activated.

400.description: The certificate cannot be activated (expired, retired too long ago, or its private key has been removed)

delete.summary: Delete a Staged or Retired SAML Certificate
delete.description: Removes the certificate from the metadata at once, for example after a key compromise. The active certificate cannot be deleted (`400`); activate or rotate to another certificate first.

400.description: The certificate is the active one

post.summary: Create OIDC 1.0 Client
post.description: Creates a confidential or public (PKCE) OIDC client. For confidential clients, `client_secret` is returned **once** in the `201` response. API clients need `can_mint_tokens` to create a confidential client that can use the `client_credentials` grant (every confidential client can while the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_OAUTH_FLOWS=1`): its access tokens carry the chosen `client_id` as their subject.

409.description: `client_id` already in use on this provider

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: OIDC Client DB UUID or OAuth `client_id`

patch.description: API clients need `can_mint_tokens` when the client, as updated, can use the `client_credentials` grant.

409.description: `client_id` already in use on this provider

put.description: API clients need `can_mint_tokens` when the client, as updated, can use the `client_credentials` grant.

409.description: `client_id` already in use on this provider

post.summary: Rotate OIDC Client Secret
post.description: API clients need `can_mint_tokens` when the client can use the `client_credentials` grant.

post.summary: Generate or Import OIDC/JWT Signing Key
post.description: Adds one key. A provider may publish at most 20 keys: the active key, unexpired keys, and expired keys still within their retention or still covering a token they signed (`409` when full; delete keys first). Expired keys that have left the JWKS do not count; this call removes them, as `prune-expired` would, and lists their kids in `pruned`. A key that is already on the provider answers `409`. Importing a private key (`keyMode: "paste"`) requires `can_mint_tokens` for API clients, because whoever holds the key can mint tokens with it.

keyTtl.description: Lifetime of this key only (at least 300 seconds); defaults to the provider's key TTL. It does not change the provider's rotation TTL unless `applyTtlToProvider` is true.

applyTtlToProvider.description: Also make `keyTtl` the provider's key TTL for automatic rotation; a non-zero rotation lead time must stay at least 300 seconds shorter than it

activate.description: Immediately promote this new key to `active_kid` (the provider `alg` follows it). `keyTtl` must then exceed a non-zero rotation lead time by at least 300 seconds, or automatic rotation would replace the key right away.

201.description: Created key metadata; `pruned` lists the kids of expired keys this call removed

409.description: The provider already publishes 20 keys, or this key already exists on it

post.summary: Delete Several Non-Active Signing Keys

400.description: The list is empty, contains the active key, or would delete every key

patch.description: Also sets the provider `alg` to the key's algorithm, so automatic rotation keeps it.

post.summary: Prune Expired Non-Active Keys
post.description: Deletes the non-active keys that are no longer published in the JWKS: past their expiry plus the provider's retention, and past the expiry of every token they signed.

get.summary: List Shared Directory Users & Custom Role Schema
get.description: Requires `user_scope` of `read` or `write` when called by an Admin API Client.

200.description: Directory users and auto-discovered SAML attribute schema

post.summary: Create Shared Directory User
post.description: Requires `user_scope='write'` when called by an Admin API Client. The user's OIDC `subject` is assigned by the directory and never taken from the request. `email_verified` defaults to `true` for users created here.

patch.description: Requires `user_scope='write'` when called by an Admin API Client. A changed `email` is marked verified unless `email_verified` is sent; `subject` never changes.

post.summary: Generate Single-Use macOS Touch ID Enrollment Link
Sign a Directory User Out Everywhere
post.description: Ends every SSO session of the user, with all providers of the directory, and revokes the user's OIDC access and refresh tokens (`offline_access` grants included) and unredeemed authorization codes, without suspending or deleting the user. Sessions that applications keep themselves are not affected. Needs a console session (with `X-CSRF-Token`) or an Admin API Client with `user_scope='write'` (`403` otherwise). Audited as `user.sessions_revoked`.

200.description: The user's sessions, tokens and codes have ended

post.summary: Mint Signed Workload / Machine JWT
post.description: Issues a signed JWT from the specified provider (`idpId`). Accepts a console session (cookie plus `X-CSRF-Token`) or a provider-scoped Admin API Client with `write` permission on `idpId` and the `can_mint_tokens` capability. The retired per-administrator legacy key (`Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) is accepted only while the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_ADMIN_API_KEY=1`, and only while its owner is still an administrator. `extra` cannot set registered claims (`iss`, `aud`, `sub`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`, `jti`), end-user authentication and session claims (`nonce`, `auth_time`, `amr`, `acr`, `azp`, `at_hash`, `c_hash`, `s_hash`, `sid`, `cnf`, `act`), or end-user identity and access-token claims (`client_id`, `scope`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `preferred_username`, `email`, `email_verified`, `phone_number`, `groups`); such names are dropped and listed in `ignored_claims`. So that a workload token cannot pass as one of the provider's own ID or access tokens, which share its issuer and keys, it has the JOSE header `typ` `workload+jwt`, lives at most 24 hours, and `aud` must not be the provider's issuer or the `client_id` of one of its OIDC clients (`400`). The operator can restore the old tokens (`typ` `JWT`, up to 365 days, identity claims, any audience) with `OIDC_LEGACY_WORKLOAD_TOKENS=1`. Every mint is recorded in the administrator audit log.

ignored_claims.description: Present when `extra` contained claim names that were dropped

BearerToken.description: Pass an Admin API Client token (`idp_adm_...`) or an OAuth2 Client Credentials access token (`idp_at_...`). `Authorization: ApiKey idp_adm_...` is also accepted on `/api/*`, but not by the SCIM 2.0 server.

ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyHeader.description: Pass `idp_adm_...` directly in the `X-API-Key` header. The SCIM 2.0 server also accepts a SCIM token (`idp_scim_...`) here.

BasicClientCredentials.description: HTTP Basic auth with Admin API Client `client_id` (`iac_...`) as username and `client_secret` (`idp_adm_...`) as password. Not accepted by the SCIM 2.0 server.

OAuth2ClientCredentials.description: Exchange an Admin API Client `client_id` and `client_secret` at the token URL for a short-lived `idp_at_...` Bearer token.

ConsoleSession.name: __Host-IDPSESSID
ConsoleSession.description: Interactive Admin Console session, created by signing in to the console (`__Host-IDPSESSID` over https, `IDPSESSID` over plain http). Browsers send it automatically on same-origin requests; scripts cannot set it. Requests that change state also need `ConsoleCsrfToken`. Required (and the only accepted credential) for Admin API Client management and the IP allowlist status and blocked-request log. The administrator audit log also accepts Admin API clients with `can_read_admin_audit`.

ConsoleCsrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
ConsoleCsrfToken.description: CSRF token of the console session (`csrfToken` returned by the console sign-in, and by `/api/me` while signed in; empty when not signed in). Required with `ConsoleSession` on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests; GET requests need only the cookie. Not used by API clients.

ScimBearer.description: Provider SCIM token (`idp_scim_<id>_<secret>`, issued at `POST /api/providers/{providerId}/scim/tokens`) for the hosted SCIM 2.0 server (`/{idpId}/scim/v2`). Its `permission` (`read` or `write`) and `filter_groups` limit what it can do. Also accepted in `X-API-Key`. Admin API Client tokens work there too when they can access the provider and have `user_scope` `read` (`write` for changes).

LegacyAdminApiKey.name: Authorization
LegacyAdminApiKey.description: Retired per-administrator legacy API key, sent as `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` (or in `X-API-Key`). Accepted only by `POST /api/token`, only while the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_ADMIN_API_KEY=1` (`legacy_admin_api_key` in config.php), and only while its owner is still listed in `users.txt`. The console no longer shows these keys; use an Admin API Client instead.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials

Forbidden.description: Caller lacks permission for the target provider or resource scope

ConsoleSessionRequired.description: Admin API Clients are rejected: this operation needs an interactive Admin Console session

delivery_mode.description: `direct` pushes over HTTPS from Cloud; `agent` relays via the On-Premises Windows SCIM Proxy Agent (`scim-agent.exe`).

bearer_token.description: Token for the target SCIM server (direct mode). Required on create, and again whenever `scim_base_url` (compared after normalization) or `delivery_mode` changes: a stored token is only ever sent to the URL it was saved with. Agent mode stores no token.

push_passwords.description: Optional: include user's password in outbound SCIM User payloads when set. Console sessions only (API clients need the operator setting `OIDC_ALLOW_API_CLIENT_PASSWORD_PUSH=1`). Needs the vault key in the environment variable `OIDC_SCIM_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, unless the operator sets `OIDC_ALLOW_PASSWORD_PUSH_WITH_KEY_FILE=1` (`allow_password_push_with_key_file` in config.php); otherwise enabling it is rejected with `400`. Only passwords set or changed while the owner has a connector with `push_passwords` on are pushed.

reset_remote_mappings.description: Deletes this connector's remote ID mappings in the same transaction; done automatically when the normalized SCIM base URL or the delivery mode changes.

actor_type.description: `system` for alerts the IdP raises itself

actor_id.description: Administrator username, or the API client's `client_id` (empty for `system`)

target.description: Id of the affected object (kid, client_id, user id, ...)

IpAllowlistStatus.description: The IP allowlist as the server applies it

state.description: `disabled`: no entry is set and every address is served; `active`: only addresses inside `ranges` are served; `deny_all`: every request is refused, because no entry is usable or because config.php sets `ip_allowlist` but does not load

enforcing.description: Requests are refused: `state` is not `disabled` and report-only is off

report_only.description: `ip_allowlist_report_only`: nothing is refused, and the requests that would be are recorded with `enforced: false`

source.description: Where the list is set: the `OIDC_IP_ALLOWLIST` environment variable (it replaces the config.php list) or config.php; `none` when neither applies, always so when `state` is `disabled`, and when config.php sets `ip_allowlist` but does not load

config_php.description: Whether config.php exists and loads; while it is `unreadable` or `failed`, none of its settings apply

label.description: Name given in config.php; empty when none

cidr.description: The block it matches, in canonical form

notes.description: For example that host bits were set, or that the block matches every address

problems.description: Entries that are ignored and why, or why every request is refused

code.description: One of `config_php_unusable`, `config_problems`, `viewer_not_allowed`, `trusted_proxy_any`, `trusted_proxy_invalid`, `forwarded_for_ignored`, `forwarded_for_missing`, `proxy_address_listed`, `everything_range`, `no_ipv6_range`, `no_ipv4_range`, `report_only`, `htaccess_outdated`, `php_display_errors`, `log_disabled` and `log_unavailable`; more may be added

viewer.description: The caller's own request as the allowlist sees it, with the decision the server makes for it

ip.description: The client address the allowlist checks; `null` when it cannot be determined (`problem`)

peer.description: The address the connection came from (REMOTE_ADDR)

via_proxy.description: `ip` comes from the X-Forwarded-For header of a trusted proxy

problem.description: Why there is no client address (see `reason` of `BlockedRequestEntry`)

decision.description: `refused` in report-only mode: the caller would be refused once report-only is off

reason.description: Why the caller is, or would be, refused

matched.description: The range that allows the caller

suggested_entry.description: An entry that would allow the caller: its IPv4 address as a /32, or the /64 of its IPv6 address; `null` without `ip`

trusted_proxies.description: The configured `trusted_proxies` entries: X-Forwarded-For is read only from these, and the allowlist ignores entries that cover every address (`/0`)

BlockedRequestsLog.description: The blocked-request log (`blocked_requests.sqlite` in the data directory)

available.description: `false` when the data directory or the file is not writable, or the file cannot be read (details in the PHP error log)

size_bytes.description: Size of the file and its write-ahead log

max_bytes.description: Size cap (`ip_allowlist_log_max_mb`): when it is reached, the oldest entries make room

retention_days.description: Entries whose last request is older are deleted (`ip_allowlist_log_retention_days`)

hits.description: Number of requests the entries count

oldest.description: First request of the oldest entry; `null` when the log is empty

newest.description: Last request of the newest entry; `null` when the log is empty

BlockedRequestEntry.description: The refused requests of one client address (an IPv6 /64), with one reason and report-only state, in one hour

address.description: Client address of the last request; empty when unknown

address_key.description: What the entry groups by: the IPv4 address, `<network>/64` for IPv6, or `unknown`

peer_address.description: The connection's address (REMOTE_ADDR) of the last request when it was not the client: a trusted proxy whose X-Forwarded-For header named the client (or was malformed), or a value that is not an IP address; else empty

forwarded_for.description: X-Forwarded-For header of the last request (at most 200 characters) when the client address came from it, or when it was refused as `bad_forwarded_for`; else empty

reason.description: `not_listed`: the address is outside every range; `bad_forwarded_for`: a trusted proxy sent a malformed X-Forwarded-For header (or more than 32 hops or 4096 bytes); `unknown_address`: the connection's address (REMOTE_ADDR) is not an IP address; `config_error`: no entry is usable, or config.php sets `ip_allowlist` but does not load; `check_failed`: the check itself failed

first_request.description: Method and path of the first request (never the query string)

last_request.description: Method and path of the last request

host.description: Host header of the last request

user_agent.description: User-Agent header of the last request

AdminTotpSetup.description: A new authenticator app secret (RFC 6238 TOTP with SHA-1, 6 digits and 30-second steps), pending until a code from it confirms it

secret.description: Base32 secret to type into the authenticator app

otpauth_uri.description: `otpauth://totp/...` URI with the same secret, for a QR code

enrolled.description: A confirmed app: every sign-in needs a code

pending.description: An app is being set up and can still be confirmed

can_mint_tokens.description: May mint JWTs at `POST /api/token`, import private signing keys, and manage OIDC clients that can use the `client_credentials` grant

can_read_admin_audit.description: May read its owner's administrator audit log (`GET /api/admin-audit-logs`)

allowed_ips.description: Normalized CIDR blocks this client may authenticate from; empty means any address. See `AdminApiClientCreateRequest.allowed_ips`.

api_token.description: Plaintext API token (returned only once upon creation or rotation)

client_secret.description: Alias of `api_token` for OAuth2 / HTTP Basic clients

AdminApiClientCreateRequest.description: Unknown values of the enumerated fields, and boolean fields (`can_create_providers`, `can_mint_tokens`, `can_read_admin_audit`) other than `true`/`false` (or `1`/`0`), are rejected with `400`.

description.example: Manages staging and QA SAML/OIDC apps

allowed_provider_ids.description: List of 1 or more Provider UUIDs or `idpId` slugs this API client may access when `provider_scope='selected'`.

can_create_providers.description: Allow creating new providers (`POST /api/providers`). Newly created providers are automatically appended to `allowed_provider_ids`.

user_scope.description: Access to the shared directory: `/api/users`, `/api/groups`, and SCIM tokens and connectors

can_mint_tokens.description: Allow minting JWTs at `POST /api/token`, importing private signing keys (`keyMode: "paste"`), and creating, changing or rotating the secret of OIDC clients that can use the `client_credentials` grant. Clients created before this capability existed do not have it (unless the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_API_CLIENT_TOKEN_MINTING=1`, which lets every client with provider `write` permission do all of this).

expires_in.description: Optional lifetime of at most 365 days (`3600`, `7d`, `30d`, `90d`, `1w`, ...), a future ISO-8601 timestamp, or `never`; anything else is rejected with `400`

can_read_admin_audit.description: Allow reading the owner's administrator audit log (`GET /api/admin-audit-logs`): every administrative action of the owner's console sessions and API clients, sign-in attempts with the owner's name, source addresses and user agents. Off by default.

allowed_ips.description: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses or CIDR blocks this client may authenticate from (also accepted as one string separated by spaces or commas). Stored normalized (`198.51.100.7` becomes `198.51.100.7/32`). Empty (the default) means any address. Checked on every request that presents the client's credential, its access tokens included, and at the client credentials exchange; a request from another address gets the same `401` as an invalid credential and is recorded in the owner's administrator audit log as `admin_client.source_denied`. The client address is REMOTE_ADDR, or the `X-Forwarded-For` client when REMOTE_ADDR is one of the operator's `trusted_proxies`. The operator's site-wide `ip_allowlist` applies first. Host names, wildcards and `a-b` ranges are rejected with `400`.

AdminApiClientUpdateRequest.description: Unknown values of the enumerated fields, and boolean fields (`can_create_providers`, `can_mint_tokens`, `can_read_admin_audit`) other than `true`/`false` (or `1`/`0`), are rejected with `400`.

allowed_ips.description: Replaces the list; `[]` allows any address. See `AdminApiClientCreateRequest.allowed_ips`.

alg.description: Signing algorithm: that of the active key (`active_kid`)

effective_key_ttl_seconds.description: Key TTL automatic rotation actually uses: the provider's value, else `SIGNING_KEY_TTL`, else one hour

effective_expired_key_retention_seconds.description: Retention actually applied: the provider's value, else `EXPIRED_KEY_RETENTION`, else one hour

friendly.description: Printable text without control characters, invisible formatting marks or repeated spaces. Together with the owner it forms the global provider ID (`idpId`): `<owner>-<name>` with every `-` of the name replaced by `_` (`staging-idp` gives `admin-staging_idp`).

default_auth_policy.description: Any other value is rejected with `400`

keyMode.description: `paste` (import a private key) requires `can_mint_tokens` for API clients

keyTtl.description: Signing key TTL: at least 300 seconds, at most 365 days

keyRotationLeadTime.description: 0, or at least 300 seconds shorter than `keyTtl` (automatic rotation generates a new key every TTL minus lead time)

expiredKeyRetention.description: How long expired keys stay published; omit to use the operator default (`EXPIRED_KEY_RETENTION`, else one hour)

key_ttl.description: At least 300 seconds, and at least 300 seconds longer than a non-zero rotation lead time

key_rotation_lead_time.description: 0, or at least 300 seconds shorter than the key TTL

active_kid.description: Also sets the provider `alg` to that key's algorithm

acs_endpoints.description: The assertion consumer endpoints actually honored: HTTP-POST only, always including `acs_url`.

persistent_id_scheme.description: Stored setting: `hmac` (keyed per provider; default for new apps) or `legacy` (apps saved before keyed identifiers existed). `legacy` takes effect only while the `legacy_saml_persistent_ids` compatibility flag is on.

persistent_id_scheme_effective.description: The derivation assertions use now: `legacy` only for a `legacy` app while `legacy_saml_persistent_ids` is on

SamlAppInput.description: A second application with the same `sp_entity_id` on the provider is rejected with `400`.

sp_metadata_xml.description: Optional raw `<md:EntityDescriptor>` SP Metadata XML. On create, the metadata provides every field and sibling fields override it. On update (refresh), only `acs_url`, `acs_endpoints`, `slo_url`, `supported_name_id_formats` and the certificates present in the metadata change; signing, encryption and verification flags, NameID settings, `attribute_mapping` and `name` are kept unless sent. The metadata entityID must match the app unless `sp_entity_id` is sent.

acs_endpoints.description: Additional indexed assertion consumer endpoints. Only HTTP-POST endpoints that use https (or loopback, unless `allow_insecure_http_endpoints` is on) are stored; `acs_url` is always included, and a replaced `acs_url` is dropped.

persistent_id_scheme.description: Default `hmac` for new apps; an existing app keeps its scheme unless sent. `legacy` is accepted only for an app that already has it, or while the `legacy_saml_persistent_ids` flag is on (otherwise 400).

sign_assertion.description: At least one of `sign_response` and `sign_assertion` must stay true (both false is rejected with `400`)

client_secret.description: Present only on creation or explicit rotation

client_secret_preview.description: `sec_••••••••` plus the last 4 characters for generated secrets; never derived from the start of a secret

grant_types.description: Flows the client may use; enforced at /authorize and /token. `implicit` allows `response_type` `id_token` and `code id_token`; response types with `token` are refused unless the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_IMPLICIT_ACCESS_TOKENS=1`. Public clients cannot have `client_credentials`.

login_uri.description: Initiate Login URI used by the end-user portal (OIDC Core section 4, third-party-initiated login). Empty means the client is not shown in the portal.

client_id.description: Unique per provider; a duplicate answers `409`

client_secret.description: Create only; omit to have a strong secret generated

require_pkce.description: Require a PKCE `code_challenge` on every authorization request that returns a code. Whenever a challenge is sent, `code_challenge_method` must be `S256`: an omitted method means `plain`, which is refused unless the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_PKCE_PLAIN=1` (then only for confidential clients without `require_pkce`) or `OIDC_LEGACY_OAUTH_FLOWS=1` (then for every client).

grant_types.description: Enforced at /authorize and /token. `implicit` allows `response_type` `id_token` and `code id_token`; response types with `token` are refused unless the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_IMPLICIT_ACCESS_TOKENS=1`. Public clients cannot have `client_credentials`.

auth_policy.description: `inherit` (the default) uses the provider's `default_auth_policy`; unknown values are rejected with `400`

login_uri.description: Initiate Login URI used by the end-user portal (OIDC Core section 4, third-party-initiated login); https required except for loopback unless `allow_insecure_http_endpoints` is set; empty means the client is not shown in the portal.

subject.description: Immutable OIDC subject (`sub`); assigned by the directory

email_verified.description: Defaults to true for users created through this API and for email changes made through it

groups_base.description: Update only. The group list that `groups` was derived from. Only the groups added or removed relative to it are applied (case-insensitive), and changes made meanwhile by others are kept; without it, `groups` replaces the list.

attributes_base.description: Update only. The attribute map that `attributes` was derived from. Only the keys changed relative to it are applied; for a list value that someone else changed meanwhile, only the values added or removed are applied. Without it, `attributes` replaces the map.

ttl.description: 1 second to 24 hours, as seconds or a duration such as `15m`, `1h` or `24h` (up to 365 days while the operator sets `OIDC_LEGACY_WORKLOAD_TOKENS=1`)

extra.description: Additional claims. Registered claims, end-user authentication or session claims (`nonce`, `auth_time`, `amr`, `acr`, `azp`, `at_hash`, `c_hash`, `s_hash`, `sid`, `cnf`, `act`) and end-user identity or access-token claims (`client_id`, `scope`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `preferred_username`, `email`, `email_verified`, `phone_number`, `groups`) are dropped.
